title: From safe research to *hireable strategy*
dek: The original pack proved diligence. This revision makes the interpretation, emotional tension, creative judgment, and paid-work boundary visible without weakening the evidence standard.
lens: Creative strategy · decision intelligence · copy elevation

sections.heading: the governing *verdict*
sections.kicker: User calibration outranks a clean machine score
sections.body:
The first pack was structurally strong and commercially incomplete. It often moved from fact to recommendation without exposing the interpretation in between, so accurate product language became safe hooks and competent scripts. Farrice's 5/10 verdict is the baseline.

The repair adds a disciplined middle: observation, pattern, labeled interpretation, plausible alternative, decision delta, and falsifier. Only then does copy craft enter. The creative now has a human pressure point to dramatize instead of a feature list to decorate.

items.why: Public-source rigor, source links, VERIFIED / LIKELY / UNCONFIRMED states, visible unknowns, test logic, visual readability, and claim safety.
Reporting-only diagnoses, generic feature hooks, emotionally flat scripts, and the missing boundary between the free proof note and paid account-informed work.
No invented buyer emotions, performance results, customer language, medical outcomes, creator experience, or causal certainty.
A founder should see one non-obvious read, understand why it is defensible, feel the buyer tension in the sample copy, and know exactly what evidence could prove the strategist wrong.

blocks.label: 1 · Diagnose
blocks.text: VERIFIED OBSERVATION → MATERIAL PATTERN → LABELED INTERPRETATION → PLAUSIBLE ALTERNATIVE → DECISION DELTA → CHEAPEST FALSIFYING TEST

blocks.label: 2 · Elevate
blocks.text: DARA owns the testable strategy. LUKE IHA turns the chosen tension into six emotionally specific openings. STEFAN GEORGI removes script dead zones and protects curiosity, recognition, and payoff. The claim gate can veto language; no specialist can change the hypothesis or upgrade an inference.

blocks.label: 3 · Split the product
blocks.text: INTERNAL AUTOPSY: exhaustive diagnosis, alternatives, complete scripts/briefs, and test sequence. CLIENT PROOF NOTE: one arresting interpretation, evidence, two territories, six sample openings, visible unknowns, and the paid-work boundary.

items.action: Rello · The routine may be the competitor
items.why: Facts became a private failure scene: the half-used tub, late Tuesday, and self-blame of another routine that did not survive the morning.

items.action: GateDrop · The category sells blast; the format can sell agency
items.why: Portability became a psychological advantage: a smaller, more reversible energy decision instead of sixteen ounces of commitment.
Clear protein became the answer to a concrete 3:17 p.m. tension between a shake that feels like a meal and a seltzer that feels incomplete.

items.action: Glow Up · Make a dense formula feel emotionally light
items.why: The ingredient inventory became sensory rebellion and a pull-tab afternoon ritual, with the formula held as proof rather than the opening.

items.action: True Sea Moss · Trust debt changes persuasion order
items.why: The responsible creative recommendation remains a hold. Current-batch operational evidence must become the proof object before benefit copy can carry trust.

blocks.label: Spine · Dara Denney
blocks.text: ACCEPTED: one job per concept, format/message separation, public evidence limits, and controlled test architecture. EVIDENCE OF CHANGE: the core brief structure and test sequence remain intact.

blocks.label: Differentiator · Analyst's Truth Standard
blocks.text: ACCEPTED: reporting now advances to interpretation, alternative explanation, decision delta, and reversal condition. EVIDENCE OF CHANGE: every brand now states what the evidence means and what could prove the read wrong.

blocks.label: Craft · Luke Iha
blocks.text: ACCEPTED: consequence-first, buyer-recognition openings replaced accurate but generic feature restatements. EVIDENCE OF CHANGE: Tuesday problem, sixteen ounces of commitment, 3:17 p.m., protein penance, and batch-number hooks.

blocks.label: Script · Stefan Georgi
blocks.text: ACCEPTED: the Rello script opens on a lived scene, withholds the product until recognition lands, then resolves with proof and a bounded CTA. EVIDENCE OF CHANGE: the half-used tub and 6:42 a.m. scene replace an explanatory product open.

blocks.label: Skipped
blocks.text: Alen Sultanic, Mitch Albom, Jason Fladlien, and additional copy routes were not loaded into the artifact. Their likely contribution overlapped the filled tension, emotion, or buyer-decision slots and would increase expert-soup risk.

sections.heading: commercial and proof *boundary*
sections.body:
THE FREE NOTE SHOWS: the quality of the research, the strategist's interpretation, two creative territories, and six sample openings.

THE PAID AUTOPSY UNLOCKS: account-level diagnosis, customer-language mining, complete concept and script batches, static and creator briefs, claim clearance, the test matrix, production constraints, and post-test interpretation.

NO EVENT YET: stronger copy is still a draft hypothesis. It has not produced a reply, account access, deposit, ad result, or client preference. Farrice's next review and live buyer behavior remain the real taste and market gates.

blocks.label: Use for the next public-source proof note
blocks.text: Build a public-source Creative Test Autopsy. Preserve source rigor, proof states, visible unknowns, and one-job-per-concept test logic. Do not stop at facts: derive one labeled interpretation, keep a plausible alternative alive, name the decision delta, and define what would reverse it. Dara owns strategy; use Luke Iha only for six tension-bearing openings and Stefan Georgi only for script/dead-zone craft. Produce an exhaustive internal autopsy and a bounded client Proof Note. Do not ship unless the client note creates private recognition, shows why the read is defensible, and clearly marks where paid account-informed work begins.
